references.text: The blood shall be put on the horns of the altar, a practice established at the consecration of the tabernacle
Description of the incense altar mentioned in Leviticus 4:7, including its horns and placement before the Lord
Parallel text describing the same ritual of putting blood on the horns of the altar and pouring the rest at the base of the burnt offering altar
The blood from the sin offering shall be put on the horns of the burnt offering altar, a similar practice
The priest shall take some of the blood and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar
Moses took the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, cleansed the altar, and poured the blood at the base of the altar
Aaron's sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar
On the Day of Atonement, the blood shall be put on the horns of the altar, describing the same type of ritual
Ezekiel describes blood that is to be put on the horns of the altar in the future temple
The book of Hebrews explains how blood was used for cleansing under the old covenant and points forward to Christ's perfect sacrifice
